newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT - AT&T Q4 earnings commentary.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - AT&T Q4 earnings commentary.

text.p: AT&T issued the following statement with its fourth qurater earnings report. The table ran in full separately. AT&T reported Q4 profits from continuing operations of $0.76 per share, compared to a loss of $0.59 per share the year earlier. First Call's analysts mean estimate was $0.79 per share.
AT&T Quarterly Profits for Continuing Operations Up 12 Percent to 76 Cents a Share

NEW YORK, Jan. 22 /PRNewswire/ -- AT&T today reported fourth-quarter income from continuing operations of $1.242 billion, or 76 cents per share. Income from continuing operations, excluding restructuring and other charges for the year-ago quarter, increased more than 14 percent from $1.088 billion, while earnings per share increased nearly 12 percent from 68 cents in the comparable 1995 period.

The year-ago period included restructuring and other charges which reduced income from continuing operations by $2.036 billion, or $1.27 per share. Income from continuing operations for the year-ago quarter, as reported, was a loss of $948 million or a negative 59 cents per share.

Income from continuing operations for the 12 months ending December 31, 1996, was $5.608 billion compared with $5.241 billion for 1995, excluding the charge. Earnings per share for 1996 were $3.47, a 5.5 percent increase over $3.29 in 1995.

As previously reported, AT&T is required to reformat its results to reflect "Continuing Operations" and "Discontinued Operations." Discontinued Operations for the 1996 fourth quarter include the results of businesses being divested -- NCR Corporation and AT&T's submarine systems and new media businesses -- as well as a gain on the sale of AT&T Capital Corporation.

Income for the consolidated AT&T, including income from operations to be discontinued and the gain on the sale of AT&T Capital Corporation, was $1.623 billion, or $1.00 per share for the quarter, compared with $1.505 billion or 94 cents per share, in the year-ago quarter excluding restructuring and other charges. As reported, including the charges, the loss in the year-ago quarter was $2.676 billion, or a negative $1.67 a share. Discontinued operations for the fourth-quarter 1995 also included the results of Lucent Technologies and AT&T Capital Corporation.

"AT&T had a record year in 1996 in the face of extraordinary challenges and unprecedented changes in our business and in our industry," said AT&T Chairman Robert E. Allen. "Income from continuing operations was a record $5.6 billion, up 7 percent from 1995. At the same time, we executed a value- creating trivestiture, spinning off Lucent and NCR to AT&T shareowners. Those companies today have a combined market value of $37 billion, far in excess of their value as part of the old AT&T."

During the quarter, AT&T began to see early-stage benefits of the actions taken in response to competitive pressures. However, the company's results were affected by higher uncollectibles in communications services, reflecting collection issues and a shift in industry-wide credit risk profiles of business customers, which led to increased fraud, delinquencies and bankruptcies. The company's recent uncollectible experience resulted in increased expense of approximately $200 million in the fourth-quarter. Roughly half of that amount was due to a significant increase in the going- forward provisioning rate with the balance, or about 4 cents per share, reflecting additional risk in the existing receivables portfolio.

"We remain committed to growing our core business, investing wisely in the future and ultimately building long-term value for our owners," Allen said. Toward that end, he said that beginning in 1997, company stock used in shareowner and employee-benefit stock-ownership plans will now be purchased in the stock market rather than issued as new shares, thus minimizing the dilutive effects of these plans on equity shareowners.

For 1996, revenue from continuing operations rose 2.7 percent in the fourth-quarter to $13.238 billion, compared with $12.886 billion in the year- ago quarter. Total 1996 revenues were $52.184 billion, a 3 percent increase over comparable 1995 revenues of $50.664 billion.

For the quarter, communications services revenue increased $529 million, or 4.3 percent from the same period last year. Communications services revenues include wireline services, wireless services as well as communications products and other services.

Wireline services revenue, which includes inter- and intra-LATA toll, network management, satellite, messaging and other network enabled services, increased nearly 3 percent for the quarter to $11.541 billion. The growth in long distance revenues came primarily from U.S. business services. Long distance calling volumes grew 6 percent over the same period in 1995 and 1.8 percent over the previous quarter.

While competitive pressure continues in the consumer business, the company noted that AT&T One Rate (SM), its recently announced simple calling plan offering 15 cents-a-minute calls 24 hours a day, seven days a week in the U.S., has been well received and is meeting AT&T's expectations for reducing customer churn.

Wireless services revenue, which includes cellular voice and data, messaging and air-to-ground, grew 18.4 percent to $937 million for the fourth quarter. Consolidated cellular service subscribers grew to 5.2 million, a 31.7 percent increase from a year ago. In addition to adding more than 1.25 million subscribers on a consolidated basis, the wireless unit ended the year with more than 900,000 digital subscribers, including 500,000 on Digital PCS, which allows new features such as caller ID, message waiting indicators and short text messaging.

Revenues from communications products and other services, which include consulting and outsourcing, on-line, and wireless product sales, were $386 million, an increase of nearly 17 percent compared to the year-ago quarter. The growth was driven by gains from wireless product sales and on- line services, including AT&T WorldNet, partially offset by a decline in value-added business services. Nine months after the introduction of WorldNet, AT&T continues to invest in the service, which now has 568,000 subscribers.

Operating income for communications services rose to $1.908 billion, an increase of more than 14 percent from the year-ago quarter excluding the 1995 charge. Operating margin increased to 14.8 percent from 13.5 percent in the same quarter last year.

Financial Services revenue decreased 32.3 percent to $374 million, primarily as a result of the securitization program instituted at AT&T Universal Card Services in 1995 to diversify funding sources as well as lower card usage and promotional pricing. At year end 1996, Universal Card Services had $6.5 billion of securitized receivables, up from $3.5 billion at the end of 1995.

Financial Services expenses decreased nearly 15 percent compared to the fourth quarter last year excluding the charge. Financial Services had an operating loss for the quarter of $4 million, as compared to an operating profit of $109 million in the year-ago quarter. The decline from the year-ago period was due to the effects of $2.5 billion of receivables securitized in the fourth-quarter of 1995. The improvement from the third quarter loss of $35 million was driven by lower operating expenses.

The unit's total managed receivables, including those securitized, total $13.5 billion. The number of customer accounts was 18.3 million and number of cards issued was 23.1 million at the end of the quarter.

AT&T's total operating expenses from continuing operations increased $226 million or 2 percent for the quarter, excluding the 1995 charge. Significant increases in network and other communications services expenses were partially offset by decreases in access and other interconnection, financial services expenses and selling, general and administrative expenses. The higher network and other communications services expenses were primarily due to growth initiatives in on-line services and consulting and outsourcing, the higher provision for uncollectibles and preparations to enter the local services business.
Operating income increased $126 million, or 7 percent, while operating margin increased from 13.8 percent, excluding the 1995 charge, to 14.4 percent.

Income from discontinued operations decreased to $219 million this quarter compared with $417 million in the year ago quarter, excluding the charge. This quarter's results include the net income or loss from NCR Corporation, as well as AT&T Submarine Systems Inc. and AT&T New Media Services. The year ago quarter also included the earnings from Lucent Technologies and AT&T Capital Corporation.

Discontinued operations results also include certain adjustments to report AT&T on a consolidated basis, such as the elimination of inter-company sales, taxes on a consolidated basis and an allocation of interest expense based on the net assets of discontinued operations. In addition, AT&T reported an after-tax gain on the sale of AT&T Capital Corporation of $162 million, this quarter.

Following an aggressive timetable that began September 20, 1995, AT&T successfully completed its historic strategic restructuring on time with the spinoff of NCR at the end of 1996. Earlier in the year, AT&T concluded the spinoff of its majority holding in Lucent Technologies to AT&T shareowners and sold its majority position in AT&T Capital Corporation to a consortium of investors.

AT&T undertook the strategic restructuring to focus its communications services, systems and technology, computer and leasing businesses more sharply on their respective markets, serve their customers better and thus position them for success -- all with the aim of providing long-term value for shareowners.
